title: Core Scientific to Fully Exit Bitcoin Mining Operations by Q4 2026
summary:
The former bitcoin mining heavyweight will transition exclusively into a high-performance computing provider by 2027, phasing out its proprietary mining operations entirely by the end of 2026. Core Scientific has already reduced its network of active miners by nearly 50% since late 2025 to accelerate the company's shift toward AI data center colocation services.

The strategic pivot follows a steep decline in the company's mining earnings, with self-mining revenue falling 79% year over year to $12.3M in the third quarter and producing a $7.5M gross loss. During the same period, Core Scientific's colocation business brought in $215.4M, accounting for roughly 93% of total quarterly revenue as the firm expands its capacity across five campuses.

Core Scientific, Once the Largest Bitcoin Miner, Plans to Fully Shut Down Bitcoin Mining by Q4 2026

Core Scientific, once the world's largest Bitcoin mining company, announced during its Q3 earnings call that it is accelerating the phase-out of its proprietary Bitcoin mining operations. The number of active miners on its network has dropped by nearly 50% compared to the end of 2025, with plans to completely shut down its mining business in Q4 2026 and operate purely as a high-performance computing (HPC) colocation provider starting in 2027. In Q3, the company's colocation revenue reached $215 million (up nearly 60% quarter-over-quarter), and its EBITDA margin expanded to 57%.
